newsItems.title: Arthur Fery's Centre Court Fairytale Reaches Wimbledon Quarter-Finals
newsItems.excerpt: Britain's Arthur Fery produced the story of Wimbledon 2026 so far on Monday, July 6, rallying from a two-sets-to-one deficit to defeat Grigor Dimitrov 7-5, 3-6, 4-6, 6-4, 7-6 (10-7) on Centre Court and become the first British wildcard in the Open era to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final. The world No. 114, who grew up a short walk from the All England Club and delayed turning professional to complete a degree at Stanford, twice recovered from a break down in the fourth set before clinching a deciding 10-point tie-break in front of an enraptured crowd that included Roger Federer in the Royal Box. Fery is also the lowest-ranked man to reach the Wimbledon last eight in 12 years and the sole British player left in either singles draw. Dimitrov, whose own quarter-final bid on this court ended in tears 12 months ago when he retired injured while leading eventual champion Jannik Sinner, twice seized control after Fery's superb opening set but could not close out the fifth. The 23-year-old, who says he experienced "doubts and dark moments" during injury layoffs, will face Italian ninth seed Flavio Cobolli on Wednesday for a place in the semi-finals and is projected to jump into the world's top 70 with at least £480,000 in prize money.

newsItems.title: Japan Sweeps All Five Titles at YONEX Canada Open 2026
newsItems.excerpt: Japan wrote badminton history on Sunday, July 5, at the YONEX Canada Open 2026 in Markham, Ontario, becoming only the fifth nation ever to sweep all five titles at a BWF Super 300 event and the first team to achieve a full clean sweep on the HSBC BWF World Tour in 2026. World No. 29 Yudai Okimoto set the tone in an all-Japanese men's singles final, dismantling compatriot Riki Takei 21-13, 21-3 after halting top-seeded Canadian Victor Lai's home-title bid in the semi-finals. Riko Gunji captured her first Super 300-or-above crown in women's singles with a three-game win over US Open champion Line Christophersen, having upset Canadian favourite Michelle Li in the last four. Japan also swept all three doubles disciplines: Hiroki Okamura and Kyohei Yamashita followed up their US Open title with men's doubles gold, Hinata Suzuki and Nao Yamakita won an all-Japanese women's doubles final over Kaho Osawa and Mai Tanabe, and Akira Koga and Natsu Saito edged Chinese Taipei's Liu Kuang Heng and Hsu Yin-Hui in a three-game mixed decider. The depth of the Japanese squad has the tour turning toward the Japan Open with renewed confidence after a dominant week in North America.

newsItems.title: Elias and El Hammamy Crown Historic PSA Season in Paris
newsItems.excerpt: The 2025-26 PSA Squash Tour concluded in style at Centquatre-Paris in June, with Peru's Diego Elias and Egypt's Hania El Hammamy lifting the season-ending PSA Squash Tour Finals titles presented by TWG Global. Elias became the first South American champion in the tournament's history, coming from a game down to defeat New Zealand's Paul Coll 7-11, 11-4, 11-6, 11-9 in 82 minutes for his 23rd PSA title and second of the campaign. Coll had started strongly after Elias received a walkover into the final when Mostafa Asal withdrew from their semi-final through illness, but the world No. 3's accuracy and sustained attacking play turned the match across three unanswered games. In the women's final, world No. 1 El Hammamy claimed her second Tour Finals crown — and seventh title of a dominant season — by beating Malaysia's Sivasangari Subramaniam 11-6, 10-11, 11-8, 11-8. Sivasangari was the first Malaysian in the women's decider since Nicol David in 2012 and pushed the Egyptian throughout, but El Hammamy found the answers in the closing stages to secure the 22nd PSA trophy of her career. Each champion collected $108,000 as the tour enters its off-season break before the 2026-27 campaign opens in August.

newsItems.title: Sun Yingsha and Matsushima Crowned at WTT US Smash
newsItems.excerpt: The WTT United States Smash 2026 delivered a blockbuster finale on Sunday, July 5, at the Ontario Convention Center in Southern California, with world No. 1 Sun Yingsha and Japan's Sora Matsushima capturing the women's and men's singles titles at the $1.55 million Grand Smash. Sun edged compatriot Kuai Man 11-9, 11-6, 9-11, 11-5, 7-11, 10-12, 11-4 in a seven-game epic for her second WTT Grand Smash crown of 2026, regaining control in the decider after Kuai twice fought back to extend the match. Kuai's resilience defined the week — she rallied from 3-1 down against Hitomi Sato in the quarter-finals and overturned a 3-0 deficit against Miwa Harimoto in the semis — and still left with women's doubles gold alongside Wang Manyu, who together beat Harimoto and Hina Hayata 13-11, 4-11, 14-12, 11-8. Matsushima seized an opportunity in a wide-open men's draw after top seeds Wang Chuqin and Lin Shidong exited in the Round of 16, defeating Felix Lebrun in the semi-finals and Vladimir Sidorenko 4-2 in the championship match. China also swept both doubles titles as Wen Ruibo and Yuan Licen rallied past Lin and Huang Youzheng in five sets, while South Korea's Lim Jong-hoon and Shin Yu-bin won mixed doubles.
